findings.title: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` listed as required but also described as replaceable by `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
findings.desc: The "Required environment variable" table and the optional table ("fallback LLM provider when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset") contradict each other; state which is truly required and whether OpenRouter alone suffices.

findings.title: Vercel filesystem limitation understated for analytics
findings.desc: CLAUDE.md notes Vercel Functions can only write to `/tmp`, so an analytics/cache write to a repo-relative path would fail with a read-only-filesystem error rather than merely "not persist"; the README should say whether such writes error out (and whether they are caught) instead of implying benign non-persistence, and it omits the LLM cache limitation CLAUDE.md mentions.

raw:
FINDINGS:
1. README.md:5-7, CLAUDE.md:71-77 | Medium | security | Deploy button creates a publicly reachable app with no auth while docs claim a single trust boundary | The new one-click Vercel deploy provisions a public URL with the owner's `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` server-side and no authentication layer, so anyone who finds the URL can spend the owner's API credits; the docs assert "one trust boundary per deployment" without telling users to enable Vercel password/SSO protection or otherwise restrict access.
2. README.md:103-119 | Low | docs | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` listed as required but also described as replaceable by `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | The "Required environment variable" table and the optional table ("fallback LLM provider when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset") contradict each other; state which is truly required and whether OpenRouter alone suffices.
3. README.md:124 | Low | docs | Vercel filesystem limitation understated for analytics | CLAUDE.md notes Vercel Functions can only write to `/tmp`, so an analytics/cache write to a repo-relative path would fail with a read-only-filesystem error rather than merely "not persist"; the README should say whether such writes error out (and whether they are caught) instead of implying benign non-persistence, and it omits the LLM cache limitation CLAUDE.md mentions.

findings.title: Deploy instructions omit that the deployment is publicly reachable with your key
findings.desc: The new "Deploy to Vercel" section tells users to one-click deploy with their own `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, but never warns that the resulting Vercel URL has no authentication, so anyone who learns the URL can drive LLM calls (and file uploads) on the owner's key/budget. Given CLAUDE.md simultaneously asserts "one trust boundary per deployment", this omission is likely to mislead users into thinking the deployment is private.

findings.title: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` labelled required while OpenRouter is described as a substitute
findings.desc: The table lists `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as the required var, but the optional table says `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` "acts as a fallback LLM provider when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset", i.e. it can replace the "required" var; one of the two statements is wrong (or the precedence rule needs stating precisely) and the deploy-button `env=` param encodes the stricter claim.

findings.title: "does not persist" understates filesystem behavior on Vercel
findings.desc: On Vercel, writes outside `/tmp` fail with a read-only-filesystem error rather than silently not persisting, so the analytics/LLM-cache paths may throw at runtime; the README (and the CLAUDE.md note) should say whether these writes error out, otherwise users will misdiagnose 500s as unrelated bugs.

findings.title: Vercel filesystem writes likely fail outright, not just fail to persist
findings.desc: The docs say analytics history "does not persist across Vercel function invocations", but a Vercel Function's filesystem is read-only outside `/tmp`, so writes to a repo-relative log/cache path will throw (EROFS) rather than silently be ephemeral; if the analytics/LLM-cache write path isn't `/tmp`-aware this wording will mislead operators debugging 500s.

findings.title: Local dev instructions never mention setting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
findings.desc: The new Deploy section documents the required key for Vercel, but "Prerequisites"/"Install and run" still list only Node and Docker, so a user running `npm run dev` locally hits LLM failures with no documented `.env.local` step (which CLAUDE.md does reference).
